newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile, EU to start free trade talks in '98 - Brittan.
newsitem.headline: Chile, EU to start free trade talks in '98 - Brittan.

text.p: Chile and the European Union will carry out an extensive review of their bilateral ties this year and will start talks next year on a free trade deal, said European Commission vice president Sir Leon Brittan.

This year there will be "an analysis of the relations between Chile and the European Union. From this analysis, we have to advance in discussions towards an accord," Brittan told a meeting of Chilean businessmen.
"Let's move forward to achieve results as soon as possible. I hope we can achieve an agreement as rapidly as possible."
Chile and the EU signed an economic cooperation pact at the EU summit in Florence in June, which Chile hopes to eventually extend to a full free trade agreement.
Brittan said one area in which Chile could advance further is in the liberalization of its financial services industry.
A sector which could present problems is the agricultural industry, he added.
The EU imposes a low tariff on Chilean exports, around two percent, and 80 percent of Chilean products enter the trade bloc tariff-free or under preferential tariffs, he said.
"Minerals, fishing products and wood-pulp continue being the big winners, but Chile has done noticeably well selling wine and other products of high added value," said Brittan.
The group is one of Chile's largest trading partners, with bilateral trade totalling $7.6 billion in 1995.
Brittan started an official visit to Chile Monday and will fly to Brazil later this week.
